system_note: Reviewed entire MR_30 inpatient record (H&P, progress notes, procedure log, orders, and discharge/transfer summary) and the applicable DRG policies for sepsis (R65.21) and acute respiratory failure (J96.01). Key discrepancies found: (1) Redundant/contradictory pancreatitis coding (K85.01 present despite clear gallstone etiology and documented infected necrosis on admission); (2) organism-specific sepsis coding and POA flags inconsistent with clinical documentation (A41.50 + B96.1 billed with POA=N despite provider documentation of Klebsiella-associated infected pancreatic necrosis and early vasopressor/ lactate-supported septic shock); (3) several POA indicators for high-severity diagnoses (K85.82, A41.50, J80) are flagged as not present on admission despite explicit admission notes. Evidence and reasoning, line-by-line: 1) Pancreatitis etiology and infected necrosis present on admission - H&P documents "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology." (History & Physical (Admitting), p.210). The admitting Active Problem List explicitly lists "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" on the admission H&P problem list (History & Physical (Admitting), p.210). The discharge/transfer summary recounts infected pancreatic necrosis due to Klebsiella treated with drainage and VARD (Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.836). Conclusion: K85.01 (idiopathic acute pancreatitis) is not supported and is redundant with documented gallstone etiology and infected necrosis - remove K85.01. K85.82 (infected necrosis) is supported and was present on admission (POA should be Y). 2) Sepsis / organism specificity and POA: The record documents high lactate and vasopressor use on admission (Critical Care Progress Note shows lactate 5.6 mmol/L and P/F 72 on 11/21/2026, supporting shock/organ dysfunction) (Critical Care Progress Note, p.562). Physician orders show norepinephrine ordered and documented as administered on admission (Physician Orders, p.19). The admission H&P and problem list document infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella (History & Physical (Admitting), p.210). The discharge summary documents "infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem ... CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16" (Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.836). Per the sepsis policy, when Klebsiella pneumoniae is identified the organism-specific sepsis code A41.53 is the correct choice (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide). The policy also requires provider documentation plus objective evidence (vasopressor + lactate >2) for septic shock (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria -> Septic Shock Confirmed on Admission Pathway). Conclusion: Replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae); mark sepsis and organism POA=Y because documentation of Klebsiella-associated infected necrosis and shock is present on admission. 3) Respiratory failure and ARDS POA: The record documents invasive airway placement on admission for respiratory failure (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation documents indication: "Respiratory failure from pancreatitis and pain" and confirms placement) (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, p.41). J96.01 validation allows presumption of hypoxemia when invasive mechanical ventilation is documented (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx, Medical Pathway -> presumption rule). ARDS and mechanical ventilation are documented in the problem list and discharge summary (Hospital Problem List, p.543; Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.836). Conclusion: J96.01 and J80 are supported and, per documentation, were present on admission - POA flags should reflect that. 4) Acute kidney injury / RRT: Orders document CRRT initiation and administration (Physician Orders: "CRRT (CVVHDF) initiation - right femoral dialysis catheter; RCA anticoagulation | ... Administered") (Physician Orders, p.19). Problem list documents AKI requiring RRT with onset 11/23/2026 and recovery later (Hospital Problem List, p.543). Conclusion: N17.9 is supported. Overall corrective actions recommended: remove unsupported/contradictory K85.01 and remove organism-specifying B96.1 (redundant when A41.53 is used); change organism/ sepsis code A41.50 -> A41.53; correct POA indicators for K85.82, A41.53 (and R65.21), and J80 to Present-on-Admission. Also remove the billed pancreatic "idiopathic" code. Recommended corrected complete diagnosis list and corrected procedure list are provided below. Citations (record & policy excerpts supporting the above observations) are in evidence_cited. Auditor: findings supported by the admission H&P, procedure notes, physician orders, and discharge summary against the cited DRG policy rules for sepsis and respiratory failure.
rationale_letter: [Provider Appeal Determination Letter] To: Medical Records/Coding Department Re: MR_30 - Inpatient stay admit 2026-11-21 / transfer 2027-03-18 - Determination: Finding Summary of Review: We audited the documentation and coding for the above stay and compared the clinical record to the governing DRG validation policies for sepsis (R65.21) and acute respiratory failure (J96.01). The medical record supports severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with infected necrosis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae and early septic shock with vasopressor requirement and elevated lactate on admission. It also documents ARDS and invasive mechanical ventilation on admission and CRRT for AKI during the early course. Finding: The billed diagnosis set contains coding and POA inconsistencies that require correction. Specifically: - K85.01 (Idiopathic acute pancreatitis with uninfected necrosis) is not supported. Imaging and the admitting H&P document gallstone etiology and infected pancreatic necrosis on admission (History & Physical (Admitting), p.210). K85.01 should be removed. - The combination A41.50 (Gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella pneumoniae as cause) is miscoded. The chart documents Klebsiella-associated infected pancreatic necrosis and sepsis; the sepsis policy identifies A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) as the organism-specific code and states the organism is embedded in that A-code (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide). Please replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53. - Present-on-Admission (POA) indicators for sepsis/ septic shock and infected pancreatic necrosis are incorrect as submitted. Provider documentation shows septic shock physiology (lactate 5.6 mmol/L, vasopressor support) and documentation of infected pancreatic necrosis on the admission H&P and problem list (History & Physical (Admitting), p.210; Critical Care Progress Note, p.562; Physician Orders, p.19). POA flags should be corrected to reflect conditions present on admission. Correction being made: We will remove K85.01 from the claim, replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53, and adjust POA flags for R65.21, A41.53 (if retained), K85.82, and J80 to reflect presence on admission consistent with clinical notes. The complete corrected diagnosis and procedure sets (as adjusted per documentation) are listed below. If you wish to contest these corrections, please provide dated, signed provider documentation that justifies retaining the original codes/POA flags (for example, explicit provider statements that infection or septic shock developed after admission and was not present on arrival). Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor
